brief:
Israel's president on Saturday chose Gadi Eisenkot to attempt forming a new government following a deadlocked election, Al-Monitor reported. Eisenkot, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's strongest rival, faces the task of building a coalition after neither politician secured a clear path to power.

The mandate represents a significant shift in Israel's political landscape, with the president bypassing Netanyahu despite his long tenure as prime minister to give Eisenkot an opportunity to break the electoral stalemate.
dek: Nov 7 (Reuters) - Israel's president on Saturday chose Gadi Eisenkot, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's strongest rival, to try to form a new government following a deadlocked election that left neither man with a clear path to power.
title: Israeli president taps Netanyahu rival to form government
